decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans, as set out in the attached schedule which forms part of this notice. 20531-PPC-XX-00-DR-DH-6001 Revision P220531-PPC-XX-00-DR-DH-6002 Revision P2DESIGN AND ACCESS / PLANNING STATEMENTReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

Prior to the commencement of the development a Construction Logistics Management Plan (CLMP) shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The Construction Logistics Management Plan (CLMP) shall address the following key aspects:a)	Detail the proposed routes for construction vehicles to access and exit the site.b)	Provide measures to minimise traffic congestion and disruptions to the surrounding road network.c)	Confirmation of discussions and agreements with the NRSWA team to secure appropriate Traffic Management Orders for any temporary restrictions or road closures.d)	Outline arrangements for the management of construction traffic, including loading and unloading arease)	Confirmation of designated times for deliveries to minimise impact on peak traffic hours.f)	Provide measures to ensure the safe passage of pedestrians and cyclists around the site.g)	Provide a site layout plan indicating the location of construction activities, storage areas, and welfare facilities.h)	Detail provisions for the storage of materials, equipment, and waste to minimise visual and environmental impact.i)	Specify measures to mitigate noise, dust, and other nuisances generated by construction activities.j)	Present a construction schedule outlining the sequence of works and anticipated duration of each phase, including the number and type of vehicles required for each stage.k)	Detail the hours of work expected for each phase and the overall duration.l)	Demonstrate compliance with health and safety regulations, including provisions for worker safety and welfare.m)	Detail measures to mitigate risks associated with construction activities, such as traffic accidents and site hazards.n)	Arrangements for wheel cleaning.o)	Measures to use operators committed to best practice, demonstrated by membership of TfL's Freight Operator Recognition Scheme (FORS), or similar.Reason: To ensure that construction activities are managed to minimise disruption to the surrounding highway network, safeguard the safety of all road users, and protect residential amenity.

The development shall not commence until a Sustainable Drainage Statement has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority should be in line with our DMD Policy SuDS Requirements. The details should include:o	The approach to excavating areas with existing rain gardens, which need to be reinstated and/or enhancedo	An approach where opportunities where rain gardens can be included in the reinstatement of trenches will be takeno	Information on how the heat network itself will not be a constraint for future rain gardens and flood alleviationReason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water to maximise opportunities for sustainable development and improve water quality.
